PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 1: PASS. Audited commit ff41550 against the current sprint file, re-read fresh. The file is unchanged since d1366fa, and no criterion asserts anything between versions. Sprint 33 is merged and closed, which satisfies the stated dependency.

R1 Met.
- In ReadingView.tsx's desktop chart, each bodies.map group now has title as its FIRST child, before the halo circle, dot, glyph and label. Hovering anywhere in the group shows the tooltip.
- The text is body.tooltip, from planetTooltip(p) in constellation.ts: "Body in Sign D°MM′" with ", retrograde" appended only when retrograde is set and the body is not Sun or Moon.
- degreesAndMinutes floors both parts, then clamps degrees to 29 and minutes to 59, so 30° and 60′ are impossible outputs.
- The chart's existing dms label now reads the same helper. For any value in [0,30) the label is byte-identical to before, so label and tooltip cannot disagree.
- Probed float behaviour: for v = 12.6, the double is actually 12.59999..., so floor((v - d) * 60) = 35 is the exact floor of the stored value. Math.floor(v * 60) would give 36 only through multiplication rounding. The chosen formula is the faithful one.

R2 Met. Each sector text glyph now has title as its first child, then the glyph character. The text is sector.tooltip, from sectorTooltip(sign) = "Sign: Element, Modality", read through two new lookups, elementOfSign and modalityOfSign. Those return entries from balance.ts's existing ELEMENT_BY_SIGN and MODALITY_BY_SIGN tables, so there is no new table. The hover target was not widened, so there is no paint-order question.

R3 Met. Both strings come from pure exported functions in constellation.ts, carried on BodyRender and SectorRender. The JSX only interpolates them.

R4 Met.
- No "use client" is added, and there is no CSS change.
- Excluding bookkeeping, the diff is exactly: ReadingView.tsx (2 title elements plus comments), constellation.ts (helpers and two fields), balance.ts (two lookup exports R2 requires) and two test files.
- The phone chart is untouched, and a test asserts it has no titles.
- Chart geometry and colours are unchanged.

R5 Met. constellation.test.ts covers:
- degreesAndMinutes at 0, 12.5667 (12°34′), 29.9999 and 29.999 (both 29°59′), plus 12.5, a sweep, and the largest double below 30;
- every PLANET_NAMES x ZODIAC_SIGNS spelling;
- the retrograde suffix only when true;
- Sun and Moon never retrograde;
- the label and tooltip agreeing;
- all 12 signs against an independently written element and modality table.
ReadingView.test.ts asserts against the rendered markup:
- title is the first child of every planet group and sector glyph;
- the forced-retrograde suffix;
- exactly 22 titles, none outside the SVG.

Ran these myself:
- npm test: 28 files, 349 tests, green.
- typecheck: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: clean.

No Human Prerequisites. No test was labelled known-failing.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 2: PASS. Audited HEAD = 3e63f94 on main. I re-read the sprint file fresh: it is unchanged since d1366fa, and the hash check at dev-done confirms it.

Why round 2: CI's build job failed lint on ff41550. app/reading/[id]/ReadingView.test.ts:18 passed children as a createElement prop, which react/no-children-prop rejects. I reproduced it: eslint on the ff41550 blob reports 1 error, exit 1.

My round-1 notes said lint was clean. That was wrong: I read the last line of the lint output instead of its exit status. I have corrected that record separately with /sprint-correct.

The fix, 3e63f94, changes test code only. ReadingView.test.ts is renamed to ReadingView.test.tsx, the createElement import is dropped, and the component renders with JSX: ReadingView with eventDate, positions and events={null}, and null as its children. A comment explains the rename.
- The assertions and describe and it blocks are byte-identical. The file still runs 5 tests, and the suite total is unchanged at 349.
- No production file changed between ff41550 and 3e63f94. The round-1 findings on R1-R5 stand as recorded.

Re-ran these on 3e63f94, checking exit status this time:
- npm run lint: exit 0.
- npm test: 28 files, 349 tests, exit 0. ReadingView.test.tsx is collected and runs 5 tests.
- npm run typecheck: exit 0.
- npm run build: exit 0.

No Human Prerequisites. No test was labelled known-failing.

Tested 2026-11-23, about 02:50 UTC, in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 1280x900 and
1280x1400.
Method, stated plainly: headless Chromium does not paint native SVG title tooltips. What
produces one is the title element of the element under the pointer. So I checked:
- each title's text and position (it is the first child);
- real mouse.move hovers to the centre of every glyph, dot, halo and label, reading the
  :hover chain up to the nearest titled ancestor;
- elementFromPoint and elementsFromPoint stacks;
- a 5x3 sample grid over each part;
- the accessibility tree.

DEFECT (low, R1): the Moon glyph is occluded by the centre date label.
- /date/1969-07-20: hovering the centre of the Moon's glyph (the ☽ text) gives :hover top
  element text "1969 · 07 · 20", which has no title. It is the svg's direct child text
  element at x=320 y=316, text-anchor middle, font-size 12, letter-spacing 0.24em,
  pointer-events auto. Only 5 of 15 grid points on the glyph reach "Moon in Libra 3°29′".
- /date/2026-12-16: the same thing with "2026 · 12 · 16". 5 of 15 points reach the Moon.
- The Moon's dot and halo still work (11 to 13 of 15 points), so the Moon is still
  reachable. But the visible ☽ glyph itself, which the screenshot shows printed into the date
  text as "07 · 2☽0", shows nothing.
- It happened on 2 of the 6 dates hovered; it depends on where the Moon falls.
- Crop: s34-crop-Moon.png.
- Fix direction: make the non-interactive centre date and time labels click-through
  (pointer-events none). That is no visual change, and lets the planet beneath receive the
  hover.

NOT a defect, recorded so it isn't re-raised: where two PLANETS overlap, the one drawn on top
takes the hover. Examples:
- 1969-07-20: Jupiter's label 00°41' sits under Uranus 00°40', and the Sun's dot under
  Mercury's.
- 2026-12-16: the Sun's label under Mercury's, and Saturn's label under Neptune's.
- 1776-07-04 and 1945-05-08: one label each.
The geometry is unchanged, the visible pixels belong to the top planet, and that planet's
correct tooltip shows.
- An early grid run flagged Pluto's dot on 1969-07-20 and 1945-05-08 as hitting a rect. A
  re-check with elementsFromPoint and a real :hover showed the top element is Pluto's own
  r=2.6 circle inside the titled g ("Pluto in Virgo 22°59′", "Pluto in Leo 7°58′"). It was
  an artefact of my mouse placement, not a defect.

PASSES.

STEP 1, planet tooltips: PASS apart from the defect.
- /date/2026-12-16 has 10 planet titles, each the first child of its g:
  "Sun in Sagittarius 24°32′", "Moon in Pisces 16°01′", "Mercury in Sagittarius 15°32′",
  "Venus in Scorpio 9°05′", "Mars in Virgo 6°53′", "Jupiter in Leo 27°00′, retrograde",
  "Saturn in Aries 7°57′", "Uranus in Gemini 2°50′, retrograde", "Neptune in Aries 1°37′",
  "Pluto in Aquarius 3°55′".
- The positions table on the same page reads:
  ☉ 24°32' ♐ | ☽ 16°01' ♓ | ☿ 15°32' ♐ | ♀ 09°05' ♏ | ♂ 06°53' ♍ | ♃ 27°00' ♌ ℞ |
  ♄ 07°57' ♈ | ♅ 02°50' ♊ ℞ | ♆ 01°37' ♈ | ♇ 03°55' ♒
  All 10 match on sign, degree and minute. The retrograde suffix appears exactly on the two
  ℞ rows, Jupiter and Uranus.
- /date/1969-07-20 also matches: "Neptune in Scorpio 26°01′, retrograde" against ♆ 26°01' ♏
  ℞, and Sun and Moon carry no suffix.
- Real hovers covered 52 points per page across 6 dates: 2026-12-16, 1969-07-20,
  1776-07-04, 2001-09-11, 1945-05-08 and 2030-03-14. Every glyph, dot, halo and label
  resolves to its own title, except the Moon defect and the planet-over-planet overlaps
  above.

STEP 2, sectors: PASS. 12 titles, each the first child of its glyph text element:
"Aries: Fire, Cardinal", "Taurus: Earth, Fixed", "Gemini: Air, Mutable", "Cancer: Water,
Cardinal", "Leo: Fire, Fixed", "Virgo: Earth, Mutable", "Libra: Air, Cardinal", "Scorpio:
Water, Fixed", "Sagittarius: Fire, Mutable", "Capricorn: Earth, Cardinal", "Aquarius: Air,
Fixed", "Pisces: Water, Mutable". All are correct. Real hovers on all 12 glyphs resolved at
1280x1400.
The first run's "none" for Gemini and Cancer was those glyphs being below the 900px
viewport, not a defect.

STEP 3, a planet over a sector: PASS. The hover target was not widened; the glyph is the
target. Where a planet overlaps a sector glyph, the planet wins:
- 2001-09-11: the Aquarius glyph centre gives "Neptune in Aquarius 6°20′, retrograde".
- 2030-03-14: the Aquarius glyph gives "Pluto in Aquarius 11°17′".
- 1969-07-20: 2 of 15 points on Scorpio give Neptune.

STEP 4, visually identical: PASS. I compared a pixelmatch at threshold 0.1 against my own
pre-sprint screenshots of the same state, taken on 902bb4c during the Sprint 33 round-2
retest.
- Desktop /date/1969-07-20 revealed, 1280x900: 1890 differing pixels out of 1,152,000, all
  in one band at x347-1104, y359-370. That band is the "Recently written" list, which now
  includes 9 November 1989, 26 December 2004 and 15 September 2008, new readings since then
  (data, not this sprint's code). Crops are c-pre.png and c-now.png. The chart area has zero
  differing pixels.
- Two consecutive current runs differ by 0 pixels.
- Phone 390x844, the same state: 10 differing pixels out of 329,160, which is anti-aliasing
  noise. The phone chart has 0 titles; that was optional and not added.

STEP 5, /reading/[id]: PASS apart from the defect. /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-
d65da32ae38d has the same 22 titles, first-child placement and table match as
/date/1969-07-20, and the same Moon glyph miss ("1969 · 07 · 20" on top).

The accessibility tree exposes all 22 titles as accessible names (role generic), for
example "Aries: Fire, Cardinal". No console or page errors.

PASS: QA1 live-loop audit of fix commit 4dbb982 (LiveQA round 1 CONDITIONAL, R1 Moon glyph occluded): PASS.

LiveQA's defect: the centre date label, text at x=320 y=316, and the hour label at y=338 are drawn after the planet groups with pointer-events auto. Where the Moon's glyph lands under the date label (1969-07-20), the label took the hover, and the Moon's title never showed.

The fix: 53229b9..4dbb982 changes app/reading/[id]/ReadingView.tsx (+7) and its test (+12), plus the state file.
- Both centre text elements gain pointerEvents="none", which React renders as pointer-events="none", with a comment.
- That is a hit-testing change only. Fill, font, position and paint order are unchanged, so there is no visual change and the R4 "no visual change" line holds.
- The planet groups and their titles are untouched.
- No "use client" or CSS change.

Is it complete? The new test asserts that both centre labels carry pointer-events="none". It also asserts that those two text elements are the ONLY elements after the last planet group in the desktop SVG, so no other later-drawn element can sit on top of a planet. Earlier siblings (sectors, aspect lines, rings) are painted beneath the planets and cannot occlude them.
